_comment: The -v2 profiles: the -v1 ones in loss_profiles.json without an rt60_s scale,
so the rt60 term never enters ambience. On a played passage the RT60
estimate largely follows note sustain: the same settings read seconds apart
through two passages, a dry render can read longer than a reverberant one,
and when it passes its confidence gate the term can reach 15 to 50
(scripts/study_rt60.py; 'The RT60 term - measured, and dropped from the -v2
They live in their own file because loss_profiles.json is frozen: every
number measured with a -v1 profile reproduces from it, and frozen listening
scores (analysis/listening.py) are checked against its hash.

unpaired-v2.description: A commercial recording against a render. Different performance, different notes, so only playing-invariant statistics are trusted. As -v1, without the rt60 term: the RT60 estimate does not measure reverb on played material.

paired-v2.description: The same DI through both sides. The performance is identical, so envelope and time-domain features mean what they say and are weighted up. As -v1, without the rt60 term: the RT60 estimate does not measure reverb on played material.
